notes: Use-case summary: midsize SaaS product search + contextual help. Primary value = faster, more relevant help search; secondary = analytics on query intent.
Workload details: - Real-time semantic search queries during peak hours (50-200 QPS); - Nightly bulk embedding job ~5M rows (ETL -> S3 -> batch embedding); - Periodic reranking for A/B tests.
Throughput & latency targets: - Embedding write throughput target: sustained 150-200 QPS; - Query latency SLO: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms for single-vector queries.

POC hosted API observations: average embedding latency 68ms (95th 140ms) under synthetic 120 QPS; vector DB (Pinecone) insert rate hit limits at 180 QPS; end-to-end search p95 ~220ms with hosted + pinecone.
POC ask: show Dedicated config with reserved GPUs for nightly batch (throughput optimized) and routing policy to fall back to cheaper model for low-priority jobs.
Security notes: require SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, audit logs retention 1 year, EU residency for subset of user-uploaded docs — legal hold in scope.
Integration preferences: want managed connector to Pinecone/Qdrant + S3-based batch ingest; prefer ability to push embeddings directly to customer VPC endpoint (VPC peering).
Cost sensitivity: high for nightly batch jobs — finance wants scenario A (hosted) vs scenario B (dedicated) TCO over 12 months. Finance asked for 3-year depreciation model for Dedicated infra.
Quote from Head of Product (J. Garcia): "If we can reduce per-embed cost by >30% and keep p99 <350ms, we'll move to dedicated capacity."
Redwood differentiators that resonated: batching suggestions, model/quantization recommendations, clear performance profiles in console. Product team liked per-route cost breakdown demo.
Potential objections: vector DB vendor lock, egress costs for vector storage, migration complexity from prototype Pinecone index to production (reindex plan needed).
Decision criteria: 1) credible throughput for 150-200 QPS embedding writes; 2) nightly batch cost < hosted baseline; 3) EU data residency support; 4) clear rollback/fallback for capacity spikes.
